newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 26.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- President Kim Young-sam will hold a summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton Thursday at the United Nations headquarters in New York.

- The ruling and opposition parties on Wednesday agreed to convene a special National Assembly session early next week to deal with political and financial reform legislation and other pending issues.
- The government will lift a ban on the importation of three types of automotive vehicles, including Jeep-type vehicles with an engine capacity of 1,000cc or less, beginning July 1.

- Six presidential hopefuls of the ruling New Korea Party issued an ultimatum to party chairman Lee Hoi-chang, their arch-rival in the nomination race, to quit his chairmanship, which they claimed interferes with the fairness of the competition.
- North Korea has notified South Korea and the United States of its formal acceptance of the four-way Korean peace talks.
- Seoul government officials predict little change in the existing bilateral relations between South Korea and Hong Kong even after it reverts to Chinese sovereignty July 1.

- The Office of National Tax Administration has announced it will launch an investigation into the sources of the 45 billion won with which Lee jae-yong, eldest son of Samsung Group chairman Lee Kun-hee, purchased convertible bonds privately issued by Samsung Electronics Co.
